key_insight: A proposed universal scaling law uses initial droplet projection area to predict key impact loadings across non-ideal droplet shapes and orientations.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for droplet morphology could improve leading-edge erosion predictions and maintenance planning for wind turbine blades.
method: Couple incompressible multiphase flow simulations with finite element analysis of blade materials.
Investigate impact dynamics for droplets with arbitrary shapes and orientations.
Relate impact pressure, loaded area, force, and peak-force timing to droplet projection area.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports positively correlated peak pressure, influential area at peak pressure, and peak force, with peak-force timing scaling inversely, but provides no quantitative validation metrics.
watch_item: Validation against measured impacts and cumulative erosion is needed before applying the scaling law to field-life predictions.
paper_title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
